label: Growth mindset
summary: Growth mindset, in Maaike's work, refers to the practice of shifting from self-doubt ('am I doing this right?') toward reflective, decision-oriented questions about your own work. It is framed as something you can actively put yourself into by examining the choices you made and why. It sits in contrast to imposter syndrome, which it counters.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike introduces growth mindset specifically in the context of lone conversation designers who are new to a still-maturing field and prone to self-doubt. Rather than defining it theoretically, she operationalises it through a concrete set of questions: what design decisions did you make, can you explain them, can you think of alternatives, and what constraints were you working with? The idea is that asking better questions replaces the paralysing need for external validation.
open_questions: How does a growth mindset hold up when there is no team or peer to pressure-test your design decisions against?
At what point does reframing self-doubt as a growth mindset risk masking a genuine need for mentorship or structural support?
